result.summary: Replaces the FreeBSD cross-compilation CI task with a native build and test run inside a virtual machine using vmactions/freebsd-vm. Keeps NetBSD and OpenBSD as cross-compiled jobs, while adjusting CI scripts and functional test utilities to run on FreeBSD hosts and silence lsof warnings.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core cross-compiles for BSD targets but does not run tests against them in per-PR CI. Regressions specific to BSD platforms reach master undetected until caught by external nightly jobs.
evidence: PR description cites recent master regressions caught in nightlies that required reactive fixes: '#36078 and #36145.'
result.scope_notes: Adds a dependency on an external third-party GitHub Action (vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1) which requires allowance in the repository action configuration.
result.changed_since_previous: Narrowed from testing FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and NetBSD to testing only FreeBSD, leaving NetBSD and OpenBSD cross-compile jobs untouched. Dropped the REST request timeout workaround from the test framework.
result.card: This PR replaces the FreeBSD cross-compile CI job with native compilation and unit/functional test execution inside a FreeBSD virtual machine. Currently, BSD binaries are only cross-compiled in PR CI, allowing platform regressions to hit master and wait for nightly builds to flag them (as seen in #36078 and #36145). Unlike the earlier draft that attempted to run VMs for all three BSDs, this version scopes native VM testing strictly to FreeBSD.

risk.why: Mistakes could break CI jobs or introduce test flakiness on FreeBSD, but cannot impact node consensus or production binaries.
